newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ trade balance improvement stalls in January.
newsitem.headline: NZ trade balance improvement stalls in January.

text.p: The improving trend in New Zealand's merchandise trade balance has now stalled, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
This follows a nine month period of continual improvement up to November 1996.

"From a peak in July 1996, the exports trend has averaged a decline of 0.2 percent per month. The trend in imports shows a small rise in January, after flattening out in December and following a fall from May to November," SNZ said.

The unadjusted value of exports for January 1997 was NZ$1.457 billion, up 3.9 percent on January 1996. Significant increases in meat and dairy produce exports accounted for most of the rise. Imports over the same period fell by 3.4 percent to a value of $1.591 billion.
A trade deficit of NZ$134 million was recorded for the month of January 1997 compared with a deficit of $245 million in January 1996.

For the January 1997 quarter, unadjusted exports were valued at $4.94 billion, up 2.6 percent on the January 1996 quarter. Dairy produce, mineral fuels and meat exports accounted for most of the increase, SNZ said.
Imports fell by 4.3 percent to a value of $5.124 billion, driven largely by significant falls in machinery and aircraft imports.
The trade balance for the January 1997 quarter was in deficit to a value of $185 million, down from a deficit of $538 million in the January 1996 quarter.

Unadjusted exports for the year ended January 1997 were valued at $21.104 billion, up 1.1 percent on the previous year. Dairy produce was the top export earner for the year with a value of $3.379 billion, up $638 million on the previous year.

Imports over the same period fell by 0.6 percent to a value of $21.343 billion. SNZ said a significant fall in aircraft imports was recorded over the year. A trade deficit of $239 million was recorded for the year ended January 1997, compared with a $602 million deficit for the previous year.
"Excluding large irregular items, such as aircraft and ships, the deficit for the latest year would have been reduced to $134 million and for the previous year to $331 million," SNZ said.
